Data and settings

Clubs are found with the Phillips and Sul (2007, 2009) log t test and clustering algorithm on the series below; β-convergence, σ-convergence and distribution dynamics use the unfiltered data.

Convergence of the whole panel

log t test on all 152 units: beta = -0.875 (s.e. 0.005), t = -159.56. The null hypothesis of convergence is rejected at the 5% level (critical value −1.65).

Convergence clubs

The clustering algorithm finds 7 clubs and 0 divergent units.

After merging adjacent clubs (PS) there are 6 clubs.

Robustness

Sensitivity: the clustering is repeated for other trimming fractions and HAC methods. ari_vs_baseline is the adjusted Rand index of agreement with the first run (1 = identical clubs, 0 = chance).

Bootstrap: 200 random subsamples of 80% of the units. A unit's stability is the share of subsamples in which it stays with its full-sample club mates; 52 units are below 0.8.

β-convergence

Average growth regressed on the initial log level (1970–2003, HC1 standard errors). A negative and significant beta means that poorer units grow faster; the half-life is reported only when beta is significantly negative.

σ-convergence

Standard deviation of log levels across units in every period, and its linear trend (Newey-West standard errors, 3 lags). Clubs with fewer than 3 units are left out.

Distribution dynamics

Income relative to the cross-sectional mean is grouped into quintile classes; the transition matrix gives the probability of moving between classes over 5 periods, and the ergodic distribution is the long-run distribution it implies.

Methods and references

Club convergence: Phillips and Sul (2007, 2009) log t test with HAC standard errors (Quadratic Spectral kernel), clustering algorithm and club merging; von Lyncker and Thoennissen (2017) for alternative merging rules. Implementation: convergence-clubs 0.1.0, a Python port of the R package ConvergenceClubs (Sichera and Pizzuto, 2019), validated against it and against the Stata package psecta (Du, 2018).

β-convergence: Barro and Sala-i-Martin (1992). σ-convergence: dispersion of log levels. Distribution dynamics: Quah (1993, 1996); mobility index of Shorrocks (1978).

Phillips, P. C. B. and Sul, D. (2007). Transition modeling and econometric convergence tests. Econometrica 75(6), 1771-1855. — Phillips, P. C. B. and Sul, D. (2009). Economic transition and growth. Journal of Applied Econometrics 24(7), 1153-1185. — Sichera, R. and Pizzuto, P. (2019). ConvergenceClubs. The R Journal 11(2), 142-151. — Du, K. (2017).
